fullPassage: Retrieval practice is a strategy of bringing information to mind by deliberately trying to recall it. Recent research in classrooms has shown that repeated testing that includes retrieval practice strengthens memory better than spending the same amount of time reviewing information you have already read does. In a recent study, one group of students read a 276-word passage on sea otters and then practiced recalling the information, a second group studied the information in four repeated 5-minute study periods, and a third group made concept maps to organize the information by linking together different ideas. The time spent studying was the same for each group. One week later, the students took a final test. Those who practiced retrieving the information had the best score on the final test. It has been proposed that trying to recall the information, as opposed to just rehearsing the information, results in the type of retrieval that is more likely to trigger reconsolidation, and this additional reconsolidation strengthens the memory.

ch: 인출 연습은 우연히 떠오르는 기억에 의존하는 전략이다.
실험에서 개념도를 그린 집단이 최종 시험에서 가장 좋은 점수를 받았다.
세 집단은 학습에 투입한 시간이 서로 달랐다.
인출을 시도하는 것이 단순 되뇌기보다 재응고화를 유발할 가능성이 크다고 제안되었다.

questions.passage: Retrieval practice is a strategy of bringing information to mind by deliberately trying to recall it. Recent research in classrooms has shown that repeated testing that includes retrieval practice strengthens memory better than spending the same amount of time reviewing information you have already read does. In a recent study, one group of students read a 276-word passage on sea otters and then practiced recalling the information, a second group studied the information in four repeated 5-minute study periods, and a third group made concept maps to organize the information by linking together different ideas. The time spent studying was the same for each group. One week later, the students took a final test. Those who practiced retrieving the information had the best score on the final test. It has been proposed that trying to recall the information, as opposed to just rehearsing the information, results in the type of retrieval that is more likely to trigger reconsolidation, and this additional reconsolidation strengthens the memory.
